body:
added 1 commit
  • 0a1ab352 - Record phase 6 of the object save fixes: built, in review as MR !29
[Compare with previous version](/max757/Luminari-Source/-/merge_requests/29/diffs?diff_id=2086172053&start_sha=429ce84b6cb310de4a1338221720db91d8444271)

**The recorded audit recipe misses CR-terminated `A` records and two-field affect lines, and the DB query cannot see prototype-granted feats**

Location: this recipe paragraph, and the world-object row of the audit table above it.

Repro on the dev copy (this worktree):

```
grep -rl $'\r' lib/world/obj              # 73.obj 321.obj 296.obj
grep -c $'^A\r$' lib/world/obj/296.obj    # 70  (73.obj: 1, 321.obj: 1)
```

`get_line()` (`src/core/utils.c:3746`) strips a trailing `\r`, so the game loads all 72 of those affects; `grep -rn -A1 "^A$"` never prints them. None of the 72 has location 49 today, so the 33 stands on dev, but the recipe written down for the next audit is blind to every `A` record in those three files (and to any file that acquires CR line ends later), and "33, the same on both sides" is not a count over all `A` records.

Second gap: `parse_object()` accepts two-field `A` lines (`src/core/db.c:4058`, `retval == 2`; 4 such lines on dev, in `1074.obj` and `20830.obj`). `"-49 132[01] "` needs a trailing space, so a two-field `49 1320` line is missed.

Third gap: `objsave_save_obj_record_db()` writes an `Aff :` line only when the affect differs from the prototype (`diff`, `src/obj/objsave.c:486-497`). A saved copy of a prototype that grants 1320 carries no `Aff :` line, so `WHERE serialized_obj REGEXP 'Aff : [0-9]+ 49 132[01] '` finds OLC, treasure and crafting edits only. That holds as long as the world grep runs first and on the world files production loads; the recipe presents the query as "a saved object's affects", which it is not.

Fix:

```
grep -rn -A1 $'^A\r\?$' lib/world/obj | tr -d '\r' | grep -E -- '-49 132[01]( |$)'
```

plus one sentence: a prototype's own affects never appear in `serialized_obj`, so the world grep is the only check for them.

**The house audit read the file copy; the game loads houses from `house_data`**

Location: this row, and the tables row above it, which lists `player_save_objs`, `pet_save_objs`, `player_save_objs_sheathed` and `object_database_bonuses` but not `house_data`.

`House_load()` (`src/obj/house.c:84-87`) opens the `.house` file only as an existence check and loads the objects with `objsave_parse_objects_db(NULL, vnum)`, the `FROM house_data` branch in `src/obj/objsave.c`. `House_crashsave()` writes the file inside the same pass but outside the transaction that rewrites the table (`house.c:185-218`): a failed commit leaves the file newer than the rows the next boot loads. On dev the two stores already differ: 59 files in `lib/house`, 44 vnums in `house_data` (9743 rows). So "Production house ... files: none" was read from a copy the server never loads.

Dev copy, checked now:

```
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM house_data WHERE serialized_obj REGEXP 'Aff : [0-9]+ 49 132[01] ';   -- 0 of 9743
```

Fix: run that query read-only on production, and add `house_data` to the audit table here, in the item and in the MR description, and to the recipe.

Adversarial review of `0a1ab3529`: two findings, both as threads on the plan's audit section. Neither changes the audit result on the dev copy; both change what the recorded recipe finds next time, and the second needs one read-only production query.

Checked against the code and found consistent:

- `wear_slot_arms_needed()`: the third arm opens `WEAR_WIELD_3`, `WEAR_HANDS_2`, `WEAR_ARMS_2`, `WEAR_WRIST_R2`; the fourth `WEAR_WIELD_4`, `WEAR_WIELD_2H_2`, `WEAR_WRIST_L2`; one arm closes the offhand weapon, both two-hand positions and the left wrist. `hands_have()` is `arm_count()` plus the vestigial arm, so an arm past four adds a hand and no position.
- `plan_second_pair()` / `perform_second_pair_attacks()`: the third-hand chain is base, haste and one candidate per `bonus_mainhand_attacks` (three at `ATTACK_CAP`, five candidates at level 30 with haste); the fourth hand is base plus Improved, Greater and Epic, four; `sp->third` is one flag set by a weapon or by a monk's empty third position with `monk_gear_ok()`, with no monk-only candidate; `sp->dual` needs a weapon. Unarmed third-hand damage goes through `compute_barehand_dam_dice()`.
- `arm_count()` is the only reader of 1320 and 1321; `race.c` grants Four Arms to Thri-Kreen alone; no class table grants Extra Arms; `can_learn` is false, so random treasure and crafting (`is_valid_craft_feat()`) cannot roll it.
- Thri-Kreen: 15 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 5 - 6 - 1 = 16.0 trait, 20.0 RP, unchanged; six lost slots match `set_race_wear_restriction()`. 30 percent of 7 / 14 / 24 / 50 against 9 and 15 gives rule 2's text.
- Help `EXTRA-ARMS` and `FOUR-ARMS`, `GAME_MECHANICS_SYSTEMS.md` and `SAVE_SYSTEMS_BREAKDOWN.md` carry no price; `grep -rn "under review" docs/` is clean; the audit result is in #1; the tag `object-save-fixes-p6` is on the remote at the head; mdformat passes; both files are ASCII with LF.
- Dev copy counts reproduce: 33 `A` records at location 49 (none 1320/1321), 1659 mob feat lines (none), 489375 / 34 / 0 object rows (none), `object_database_bonuses` 2894 rows (none at location 49), 0 player files with 1320 or 1321.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/max757/Luminari-Source/-/merge_requests/29/diffs?diff_id=2086621504&start_sha=0a1ab35299d86bd96ad5addb824cd1707ed897f5#679278dcd5aa63659701b028f7995a74a67f04e4_746_746)

added 3 commits
  • 5b2917cd - Audit house_data, the table House_load() reads, for arm feats
  • f4c5c962 - Take two-field and CR-terminated affect records in the audit recipe
  • e6c85bf5 - Record the review of phase 6: two findings, fixed
[Compare with previous version](/max757/Luminari-Source/-/merge_requests/29/diffs?diff_id=2086621504&start_sha=0a1ab35299d86bd96ad5addb824cd1707ed897f5)

Fixed in `f4c5c9624`, with one correction to the premise and one to the proposed command.

**Two-field lines**: reproduced on both sides, the same four (`1074.obj` lines 10, 12, 14 and `20830.obj`, all `1 1` or `17 1`), none at location 49. The recipe now ends the feat with `( |$)`.

**Prototype affects**: confirmed in `objsave_save_obj_record_db()`, the `diff` test. The recipe now says a prototype's own affects never reach `serialized_obj`, so the world grep, on the files production loads, is the only check for them.

**CR-terminated `A` records**: none exist, on either side. Each of `73.obj`, `321.obj` and `296.obj` holds exactly one CRLF line, a room description, and no `A\r` header (Python, `d.count(b"\nA\r\n")` is 0 over all 769 files on both hosts; GNU grep `-c -E '^A[[:cntrl:]]$'` is 0 on production). The 70 / 1 / 1 came from the development `grep`, which is ugrep 7.8.4: it breaks a pattern at a CR, so `$'^A\r$'` counted something else (`^A` alone matches 10 lines of `296.obj`). The gap in the recorded recipe is still real, since `get_line()` strips a trailing CR and GNU grep's `^A$` would not match such a header, so the recipe takes it.

**The proposed command does not work where the audit runs.** Bash decodes `\?` inside `$'...'` to a plain `?`, so `$'^A\r\?$'` is the pattern `^A<CR>?$`, and under GNU grep 3.11 on production it matches nothing: run there, it gave 0 against the old recipe's 33. Under ugrep it happens to work, for the wrong reason. The recorded form is

```
grep -rn -A1 -E '^A[[:cntrl:]]?$' lib/world/obj | tr -d '\r' | grep -E -- '-49 132[01]( |$)'
```

which gives 33 location-49 records on both hosts (GNU grep and ugrep) and none for 1320 or 1321, so the table's 33 is now the count the recipe makes. The record notes why the class rather than a CR in the pattern.

Fixed in `5b2917cd4`. Confirmed: `House_load()` opens the `.house` file only as its existence check and loads from `house_data`; `Crash_load()` likewise reads `player_save_objs`, so neither file store is what the game loads.

Run read-only on production (`d5cd6a735`), as the game user, through a temporary client file removed afterwards:

```
SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT vnum) FROM house_data;                                      -- 7951, 44
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM house_data WHERE serialized_obj REGEXP 'Aff : [0-9]+ 49 132[01] ';     -- 0
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM house_data WHERE serialized_obj REGEXP 'Aff : [0-9]+ 49 ';             -- 282
```

The development copy agrees: 9743 rows over 44 houses, 0 and 301. Both sides have 59 `.house` files.

`house_data` is now a row of the audit table in the plan, in the item's note and in the MR description, and in the recipe's list of tables; the files row says what the game does with those files.

Review of `0a1ab3529` addressed; both threads answered and resolved. No change to the audit result or the prices: the two findings corrected what the record says and how the next audit runs.

| Thread | Commit | What changed |
| -- | -- | -- |
| House audit read the file copy | `5b2917cd4` | `house_data` queried read-only on production (7951 rows, 44 houses, none with 1320/1321) and on the development copy (9743, 44, none); the row is in the plan's table, the item's note and the description; the recipe lists the table; the files row says the game only checks that the files exist |
| Recipe misses two-field and CR-terminated `A` lines, prototype affects | `f4c5c9624` | recipe takes both forms with `'^A[[:cntrl:]]?$'` and `( |$)`, and says a prototype's own affects never reach `serialized_obj`; the two-field lines reproduce (four, none at location 49), the CR-terminated headers do not exist on either side (the 72 were an ugrep artifact), and the proposed `$'^A\r\?$'` matches nothing under production's GNU grep, so the recorded form differs from the proposed one |
| Record | `e6c85bf50` | `### Review 2026-10-08` in the plan |

Verification:

- The recorded recipe on both hosts: 33 location-49 `A` records, none 1320 or 1321.
- `python3 scripts/ci/local/run.py --base gitlab/master` on `f4c5c9624`: 33 of 33 jobs pass (218 s).
- The format, hygiene and secrets jobs pass on `e6c85bf50`.
- `pre-commit run mdformat` passes; the plan is ASCII with LF.

Git: no rebase, no squash, no new tag. The hand-off tag `object-save-fixes-p6` stays on `0a1ab3529`, the three commits follow it, and the project merges with a merge commit (`squash` off). Ready to merge at `e6c85bf50`.

Merged on 2026-10-08 as merge commit `294d5f20f`. Its parents are `55c934d5c` and `e6c85bf50`, and
its tree is the reviewed head's, so every hash quoted here is on master. Branch commits were not
rebased or squashed. #1 is closed, and GitLab deleted the source branch.

- Plan close-out: `b8951c3aa` on master retires
  `docs/ongoing-projects/object-save-fixes-and-arm-pricing.md`, as its Closing section says,
  now that all seven phases are merged and their items closed.
- The tag `object-save-fixes-p6` stays on `0a1ab3529`, the commit handed to review.
- No deploy: the fixes of phases 1 to 5 and 7 reach production with the next release, whose
  copyover needs its own approval.
